output.methodChoice: Collected X12 (yield by admission round) and X15 (yield by scholarship tier). Both were chosen to separate the scholarship explanation (H2) from the portal-delay explanation (H1).
output.brief: The main cause of the enrolment drop looks like the Fall 2026 scholarship cut, not the Admissions Office. The yield fell most where awards were cut: Dean's tier (45% to 32%) and Merit tier (45% to 32%). The Presidential tier, whose award was unchanged, held steady (37% to 36%), and students with no merit award fell only slightly. Early-action admits, who received decisions on the old system and timetable, also lost yield by about the same amount as regular-decision admits, so the portal delay does not explain the drop. Applications and admits both rose, so a weaker pool is unlikely. I am moderately confident, not certain: this is tier-level data, not individual-level proof, and I have not yet checked the merit-review staffing or the missing-transcript problem. Next steps: take the scholarship schedule back to the finance committee with a modelled trade-off before next cycle's award letters go out, and set a turnaround target for regular-decision files. Do not replace the Director on this evidence. Do not rebuild the portal module until the transcript problem is confirmed.
